memory_candidates.content: In bash, a resolver function that must be able to refuse via `exit N` should never be called inside `$(...)` command substitution: `exit` inside a command-substitution subshell only terminates that subshell, so the refusal's exit code never reaches the calling script's own exit status (it silently continues with exit 0). Fix: have the resolver set a global variable and call it as a plain statement, never captured via `$(...)`.

To resolve a git branch's configured remote without ever typing the literal word 'upstream' (useful when a static-assertion suite forbids hardcoded remote/branch-name literals including that word), use `git config --get branch.<name>.remote` instead of `<branch>@{upstream}` ref syntax -- same information, no literal keyword in the source.

sapience_notes.subject: Claude Code harness Bash tool auto-backgrounding threshold
sapience_notes.value: A foreground Bash tool call that produces no stdout/stderr for roughly 180 seconds gets auto-converted to a backgrounded task by the harness, regardless of the `timeout` parameter's value (observed at timeout=290000ms and again at timeout=540000ms, both converted at ~180s). Raising the `timeout` parameter alone does not prevent this; the trigger is output silence, not elapsed time against the timeout ceiling.

sapience_notes.subject: verify-touched.sh scoped check duration under a busy multi-task session
sapience_notes.value: A Batch Gate Deferral scoped verify-touched.sh invocation (no arguments) for a registration-surface-touching phase (manifest.json, suite-classification.data) selected 139+98=237 suites across two internal run-all.sh invocations and took roughly 15 minutes wall-clock in a session with ~20 concurrent sibling dispatches, dominated by a handful of load-sensitive serialized suites (test-state-write-concurrency.sh, test-state-write-regen-timing.sh, test-four-tier-conflict.sh, test-run-all-parallel.sh, test-gate-lock.sh) that it explicitly runs outside the parallel pool.

sapience_notes.subject: review_base declaration decision for the stack-PR-submission task
sapience_notes.value: The bottom PR of a review-branch stack merges into a declared review_base distinct from the integration branch (a new top-level .claude-extensions.json key, beside integration_branch), per a relayed user answer in cycle 9. A repository whose integration branch would also be its review base gets a refusal and no PRs prepared, rather than silently substituting the integration branch.

sapience_notes.subject: run-all.sh output buffering under a detached background invocation
sapience_notes.value: run-all.sh's own stdout appears to buffer heavily when invoked via nohup with stdout/stderr redirected to a file: a log file can sit static for 10+ minutes mid-run with no new [RUN]/[PASS] lines even though many suites are completing internally, then emit a large burst of buffered lines once the whole invocation finishes. Liveness must be checked via the process's own PID (kill -0), never inferred from log-file growth.

sapience_notes.subject: cslib /pr command's portability for the stack-PR-submission task
sapience_notes.value: The cslib extension's /pr command (the only existing PR-stacking machinery in this repository) was ruled not portable to core: it is prose run by a model, creates branches by checkout (forbidden by the ref-plumbing-landing concurrency-safety property in a shared working tree), and resolves bases via a forge read rather than a local manifest. core's review-stack-prepare.sh is therefore its own small implementation (decision PD2), reusing only two ideas from /pr: a chained base as the stacking primitive, and a 'Relationship to other PRs' body section.
